recipe_cards.name: Sausage & Gravy with Pasta
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Heat olive oil in your biggest, heaviest pot. Brown the sausage on all sides, don't crowd it, work in batches if you have to. Take it out, soften the onions with a pinch of salt, then garlic till you smell it. Stir in the tomato paste and cook it for a minute so it loses that raw tin taste. Crush the San Marzanos by hand right into the pot, add your bay leaves, and bring it up. Nestle the sausage and the pork back in, lid on, lowest heat you got, three hours. Stir every twenty minutes or the bottom will burn and you'll cry. If you're using dried basil instead of fresh, I don't want to know about it.

variations.name: Sunday Gravy alla Vodka
variations.twist: Ladle out a cup of finished sauce, simmer with a splash of vodka, then stir in heavy cream and Parmigiano for a rich, silky variation

variations.name: Ragù Napoletano with Braciole
variations.twist: Roll thin beef slices around pine nuts, raisins, and parsley, tie them up, and braise in the Sunday sauce for a traditional Neapolitan feast

variations.name: Spicy Arrabbiata Sunday Gravy
variations.twist: Double the garlic, add a generous pour of crushed red pepper flakes, and finish with fresh parsley for a fiery, garlicky version

groups.merge_action: brown all sides in batches, 8 min total (remove)
sauté onion 5 min, add garlic and flakes 1 min, stir in paste 1 min
deglaze with wine, add tomatoes, bay leaves, basil, rind

final_steps: bring to boil then reduce to lowest simmer
lid on, cook 3 hours stirring every 20 min
taste and season with salt and pepper

groups.merge_action: boil salted water, cook pasta to al dente

final_steps: toss pasta with a few ladles of sauce
serve with meats on the side and grated Pecorino

recipe_cards.name: Babo Pasta (Homemade Spinach Pasta with Egg Yolks)
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Blanch the spinach for thirty seconds, shock it in ice water, then squeeze it dry. I mean really dry, wring it like a dishrag. Blend the spinach with the yolks and salt until it's smooth and green as a garden. Make your well in the flour and pour the green mixture right in the middle. Pull the flour in with a fork, then get your hands in there and knead for a good ten minutes until the dough is smooth and springs back when you poke it. Wrap it up, let it rest half an hour. Roll it thin, cut your ribbons, and cook them in boiling salted water for just two or three minutes. Anyone who overcooks fresh pasta in this house answers to me.

variations.name: Beet Pasta Dough
variations.twist: Replace spinach with roasted and pureed beets for a vivid magenta dough with earthy sweetness

variations.name: Saffron Egg Yolk Pasta
variations.twist: Skip the spinach, steep a pinch of saffron in the yolks for a golden, aromatic dough that pairs beautifully with butter and sage

variations.name: Squid Ink Pasta
variations.twist: Swap spinach for squid ink to get dramatic black noodles with a subtle briny, oceanic flavor

ingredients.prep: blanched 30 sec, ice bath, squeezed dry

groups.merge_action: pour spinach-yolk mixture into well, incorporate with fork

final_steps: knead 8-10 min until smooth and elastic
roll thin and cut into tagliatelle or pappardelle

recipe_cards.name: Grilled Chicken Thighs
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Whisk the soy sauce, olive oil, honey, garlic, vinegar, mustard, and spices together in a bowl. Put the chicken thighs in and make sure every single piece is coated. Into the fridge for at least two hours, overnight if you can plan that far ahead. Get your grill hot, medium-high, and oil the grates so the chicken doesn't stick. Six or seven minutes per side, don't press down on them with the spatula like some kind of sandwich. Let them rest five minutes before you cut into them. Chicken is simple, but simple done right is better than fancy done wrong.

variations.name: Tandoori Grilled Chicken
variations.twist: Marinate in yogurt with cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala for tender, smoky, warmly spiced thighs

variations.name: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
variations.twist: Use a bold marinade of allspice, Scotch bonnet peppers, thyme, ginger, and citrus for fiery Caribbean flavor

variations.name: Chimichurri Grilled Chicken
variations.twist: Grill simply with salt and pepper, then drench in a fresh parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, and olive oil sauce

recipe_cards.name: Homemade Pizza
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in your big bowl. Add the warm water and olive oil, stir until it comes together, then dump it out and knead five minutes until smooth. Oil the bowl, put the dough back, cover it, and let it rise for an hour or until doubled. Punch it down, divide into three balls, cover with a damp towel, and let them rest another hour. Stretch each ball out with your hands, not a rolling pin. Top with sauce, good mozzarella, and whatever makes you happy, but don't be greedy or you'll get a soggy mess. Hottest oven you've got, ten minutes, and watch for the cheese to bubble and brown.

variations.name: Detroit-Style Pan Pizza
variations.twist: Press dough into an oiled rectangular pan with cheese pushed to the edges for caramelized, crispy frico corners

variations.name: Grandma-Style Sheet Pan Pizza
variations.twist: Bake on an oiled sheet pan for a thin, crispy, focaccia-like crust topped with fresh mozzarella and sauce on top

variations.name: Grilled Pizza
variations.twist: Stretch dough thin, grill one side until charred, flip, top quickly, and close the lid for a smoky, blistered crust

engineer_table.preheat: as hot as your oven goes (475-550°F / 250-290°C)

groups.merge_action: add to dry, stir until shaggy dough forms
spread sauce, then cheese, then toppings on stretched dough

final_steps: top and bake 10 min until bubbly and golden

recipe_cards.name: Buttermilk Waffles (Breakfast for Dinner)
recipe_cards.nonna_says: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a big bowl. In another bowl, beat the eggs, then stir in the buttermilk, melted butter, and vanilla. Pour the wet into the dry and stir just until combined, a few lumps are fine. If you overmix these, you'll get tough little hockey pucks and nobody wants that. Let the batter rest five minutes while the waffle iron heats up good and hot. Cook until deep golden, not pale and sad. Serve them straight off the iron or keep warm in a low oven on a wire rack so they stay crispy.

variations.name: Overnight Yeasted Waffles
variations.twist: Mix batter with yeast the night before for extra-tangy, impossibly crisp waffles with complex flavor

variations.name: Cornmeal Buttermilk Waffles
variations.twist: Swap half the flour for cornmeal for a rustic, crunchy waffle that pairs perfectly with fried chicken and honey

variations.name: Chocolate Chip Waffles
variations.twist: Fold in mini chocolate chips and a tablespoon of cocoa powder for a decadent dessert-for-dinner waffle

ingredients.item: maple syrup, fresh berries, whipped cream

final_steps: fold wet into dry until just combined (lumps OK)
pour 1/3 cup per waffle onto hot iron
cook until deep golden and crisp, about 3-4 min
serve immediately or hold on wire rack in 200°F oven
